title: Symphony No. 5
hook: From a funeral march to a love song to laughter.

painting.title: Death and Life
painting.pairingNote: Mahler’s Vienna in paint, and the symphony’s own journey in one image, from the figure of death to an embrace.

facts: Written in the summers of 1901 and 1902. Between them, Mahler nearly died of a haemorrhage, met Alma Schindler, and married her. He conducted the premiere on 18 October 1904 in Cologne.
Five movements grouped in three parts: Part I (movements 1 and 2), Part II (movement 3), Part III (movements 4 and 5).
The fourth movement, the Adagietto for strings and harp, is widely thought to be a love letter to Alma. It became world famous through the film “Death in Venice”.
The symphony has no single home key. It begins in C-sharp minor and ends in D major.
bigPicture.inOneLine: mourning (I), rage (II), life returning (III), love (IV), joy (V).

movements.heading: Trauermarsch
movements.title: Trauermarsch (Funeral March)
movements.summary: A funeral procession, opened by a solo trumpet. Twice the measured march is torn apart by outbursts of grief.

stops.hear: A solo trumpet: three short notes and a long one, climbing
stops.happening: The fanfare. Its rhythm recalls the motto of Beethoven’s Fifth

stops.hear: The full orchestra crashes in
stops.happening: The procession begins

stops.hear: A weary, song-like melody in the violins and cellos
stops.happening: The march theme itself

stops.hear: A sudden eruption: the trumpet shrieks over churning strings
stops.happening: The first outburst. Mahler marks it “Suddenly faster. Passionate. Wild”

stops.hear: The trumpet fanfare, then the march in the woodwinds
stops.happening: The procession resumes

stops.hear: A quieter, grieving melody in the strings that swells to a climax and collapses
stops.happening: The second episode

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The fanfare fades, first on trumpet, then on flute; one soft thud from the low strings
stops.happening: The procession disappears into the distance. The final note is [[pizzicato|pizzicato]]

movements.heading: Stürmisch bewegt
movements.title: Stürmisch bewegt (Stormy, with greatest vehemence)
movements.summary: The grief of the first movement turns to fury. Storms alternate with slow laments, and near the end a vision of triumph appears and vanishes.

stops.hear: Snarling basses, shrieking woodwinds
stops.happening: The storm

stops.hear: The tempo drops; cellos sing a slow lament
stops.happening: A melody from the first movement’s funeral march returns

stops.hear: Cellos alone, very quietly, over a soft drum roll
stops.happening: A long, bare [[recitative|recitative]]. The loneliest passage in the symphony

stops.label: Middle
stops.hear: Storm and lament keep interrupting each other
stops.happening: The two moods fight for control

stops.hear: Brass ring out in a bright, glorious hymn
stops.happening: A [[chorale|chorale]] in D major. For a moment, victory seems to have arrived

stops.hear: The hymn crumbles; the storm returns, then scatters into fragments
stops.happening: The vision fails. It will come back in the finale

stops.label: Last seconds
stops.hear: Quiet scraps and a soft drum tap
stops.happening: The movement evaporates

movements.heading: Scherzo
movements.title: Scherzo
movements.summary: The longest movement and the hinge of the symphony. After death and rage, life comes back as a huge, swirling dance, with a solo horn in the leading role.

stops.hear: Four horns call out; a solo horn leads a bouncing country dance
stops.happening: The [[scherzo|scherzo]] theme, a robust [[landler|Ländler]]. The horn has an [[obbligato|obbligato]] part all the way through

stops.hear: A softer, more elegant waltz in the strings
stops.happening: The first trio. City manners after country ones

stops.hear: The music stops; the solo horn calls and others answer across silences
stops.happening: Horn calls echoing as if across mountains

stops.hear: Strings pluck a shy little waltz
stops.happening: A [[pizzicato|pizzicato]] episode, tentative and intimate

stops.hear: The dances return and pile on top of one another
stops.happening: Mahler combines his themes with great contrapuntal skill

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The pace turns frantic; a wooden clapper rattles
stops.happening: A wild close

movements.heading: Adagietto
movements.title: Adagietto
movements.summary: Strings and harp alone. A melody that seems to hold its breath, always delaying its arrival.

stops.hear: Slow harp notes; violins enter with a melody that hangs in the air
stops.happening: The main theme. Each phrase leans on a note that does not belong, then resolves

stops.hear: The harp falls silent; the music grows more restless and climbs higher
stops.happening: The middle section, moving through distant keys

stops.hear: The violins slide slowly downward from a great height
stops.happening: A long [[glissando|glissando]] back to the main theme

stops.hear: The opening melody returns with the harp
stops.happening: The return

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: One last swell, and a long-held chord that takes its time to settle
stops.happening: The final resolution, delayed as long as possible

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Bernstein takes the movement very slowly. Other conductors play it in under eight minutes, which makes it sound more like a song and less like an elegy.

movements.heading: Rondo-Finale
movements.title: Rondo-Finale
movements.summary: The Adagietto’s last chord has hardly faded when a single horn note opens a new world. A sunny, bustling [[rondo|rondo]] full of [[fugue|fugue]]s, in which the love song returns as a dance and the lost hymn finally arrives.

stops.hear: One horn note; then bassoon, oboe and clarinet trade little phrases
stops.happening: A pastoral introduction. These scraps are the building blocks of the whole finale

stops.hear: Horns in a relaxed, genial melody
stops.happening: The main rondo theme

stops.hear: Cellos start a busy, running tune that the other strings take up in turn
stops.happening: The first [[fugue|fugue]]

stops.hear: A graceful melody in the strings, light on its feet
stops.happening: The Adagietto theme, transformed from a slow love song into a quick dance

stops.label: Middle
stops.hear: The rondo theme, the fugue and the dance tune keep coming round, each time more elaborate
stops.happening: The movement builds in waves

stops.hear: The brass ring out the glorious hymn
stops.happening: The [[chorale|chorale]] that collapsed in the second movement returns, and this time it holds

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: A breathless, accelerating dash
stops.happening: Laughter at the end of a symphony that began with a funeral

threads.title: The long journey
threads.body: Funeral march to joyful finale, C-sharp minor to D major.

threads.title: Themes that travel
threads.body: The second movement quotes the first; the finale transforms the Adagietto; the chorale glimpsed in the second movement is achieved in the fifth.

threads.title: The trumpet’s rhythm
threads.body: Three short notes and a long one, a deliberate echo of Beethoven’s Fifth.
